title: Decompose ingress pipeline into Ack and Visibility channels to reduce head-of-line blocking
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current ingest/ingress path couples acknowledgement (ack/nack) with visibility semantics and retry orchestration. When a worker stalls or takes a long tail due to model latency or downstream timeouts, backpressure and retries propagate to the upstream queue, causing head-of-line blocking for unrelated messages and spiking p99 end-to-end latency. This is particularly visible on bursty tenants and during model cold starts.

Goal: Decompose the ingress pipeline into two logical channels: a lightweight Ack channel that confirms receipt and allows upstream progress, and a Visibility/Lease channel that manages redelivery timing, retry budgets, and lease renewals. The decomposition should preserve correctness (no lost messages, bounded duplicate deliveries) while improving throughput and reducing p99 latencies for healthy workers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ingress can ack messages within 5ms median independent of downstream processing time.
- Visibility/lease manager handles renewals and redeliveries asynchronously with configurable timewheel defaults.
- End-to-end p99 for message processing decreases by at least 30% on representative workloads.
- No regressions in at-least-once delivery guarantees; documented duplicate window and mitigation patterns.
- Feature behind feature-flag and can be toggled per-cluster/tenant.
- Integration tests for Redis and Kafka ingress paths added to CI.
technical_notes:
Design choices considered:
1) Lease model: use a short-lived lease token stored in Redis (hash + TTL) vs using Redis streams consumer groups' pending entries. Chosen: tokenized lease + timewheel to allow explicit renewals and a clear visibility timeout.
2) Ack path: implement an ultra-thin ack RPC to the ingest router that only records receipt and sequencing metadata; worker processing returns to separate visibility manager for commit.
3) Retry semantics: introduce a retry-budget window per message that decays on repeated failures; use jittered exponential backoff for redelivery.
4) Exactly-once trade-offs: we accept at-least-once with idempotency helpers (idempotency keys and idempotent commit API) to avoid expensive 2PC.
5) Kafka vs Redis: abstract the visibility layer behind a small interface so both Kafka consumer groups and Redis streams can plug in. For Kafka we will use consumer offsets + an external visibility table; for Redis we will use a hash+TTL approach.
6) Metrics: add inflight_count, ack_latency_ms, lease_renewals, redeliveries_per_min, head_of_line_blocking_rate.

Implementation notes: timewheel library (we will vendor and pin to the upgraded fork) + upgraded redis client (v7.3) to get non-blocking timeouts and improved cluster pipelining. Avoid synchronous blocking I/O in the ack path; use netty-backed async client for Redis/Kafka coordination.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge feature-flagged implementation behind cluster-level flag; run unit + integration tests.
2) Canary deploy to staging namespace with synthetic replay traffic for 48h.
3) Enable on a low-traffic production tenant (canary tenant) for 24h and validate metrics (ack latency, p99 processing).
4) Gradually enable by region and tenant buckets, monitoring for increased duplicate deliveries or unseen latencies.
5) If any of the rollback triggers fire (redelivery rate > 5x baseline, p99 tail regressions > 20%, consumer CPU > 80% for sustained 5m), flip the flag and rollback.
6) After 2 weeks of stable canaries, enable for all tenants and remove feature flag in a minor release.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for ack/visibility separation logic and timewheel edge cases.
- Integration tests: Redis streams + Kafka consumer with simulated worker stalls and failures.
- Load test: target 10k msg/s per node, validate ack median <5ms and p99 processing drop >=30%.
- Chaos tests: randomly kill workers and introduce network partitions to validate no lost messages.
- Regression test: verify existing DLQ/poison message handling flows still operate.
- Add synthetic validator that replays a 72-hour production trace into staging.
